recipes.name: Garden Pasta Salad
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup cucumber, peeled and thinly sliced
1.5 (16 ounce) bottles Italian-style salad dressing, or to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil; cook pasta at a boil until tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes. Rinse under cold water, and drain.

Mix tomatoes, celery, carrots, bell pepper, cucumber, and onion together in a large bowl. Add cooled pasta, salad dressing, and Parmesan; mix until well combined. Cover and chill for 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Garden Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This chilled garden pasta salad is loaded with crunchy vegetables, flavored with nutty Parmesan cheese, and tossed in your favorite Italian-style salad dressing.

video.description: Watch how to make a spiral pasta salad with garden fresh veggies.

review.reviewBody:
This is almost identical to what I make. I read a review that the Italian dressing was overkill. I would like to suggest that you allow people to add their own dressing. We also serve the parmasean cheese on the side, because people like different amounts. 

We found that "Newman's Own" Oil and Vinegar is especially well liked by most people. If you like it a bit spicier, try the salad seasoning you find in the herbs & spices section as well. Also, we find that halved cherry tomatoes are prettier and often have more flavor than most tomatoes we get up north. Also, you can try sliced black olives for color contrast & variety. 

It's really a great recipe though, both as suggested and with your own touches. People have varied tastes and by letting them add their own seasoning, they can adjust amounts with ease. You won't have the chance to "marinate," but for company, dieters, diet-restricted, and/or a husband like mine (who won't use dressing at all), it's essential!

I took this to a pot luck over the weekend and it was a HUGE hit. I doubled the recipe and didn't have a bite left (approx 20 people). I didn't measure any ingredients, I just added veggies until it looked right. For the double recipe I only used one bottle of dressing. Two would've worked but it would've been much too oily for me. I'll be making this again at the request of the other guests!!

Good recipe and easy to toss together! From experience, 2 bottles of dressing are too much even when using regular pasta. Recipe is very flexible to add as much dressing as you like or add other veggies too. If making the day before, add less dressing initially (8oz), toss salad, add more dressing just before serving, toss again. I lightly sautéed some frozen broccoli and let cool before adding to the pasta; used 1 yellow bell pepper and 1 cucumber (small). Made this GLUTEN FREE (GF) by using GF Fusilli pasta (Aldi “live Gfree” brand) and Walden Farms Italian dressin. GF Pasta Tip: Bring water in large pot to a boil with 1 tbsp salt; add pasta to the water along with 1 tbsp olive oil; set your timer for 2 minutes before recommended cook time. Stir frequently the first few minutes of cooking. When pasta is al dente (taste test your GF pasta and adjust cook time by 1 minute only—quick to overcook and bad if really under cooked), strain and rinse pasta in colander with cold water. Transfer to a bowl and toss pasta with a couple swigs olive oil. Cover with plastic wrap and leave out at room temp. Then, prep your veggies and add to bowl with 4 oz. dressing; toss salad, cover bowl and place in fridge to chill. To serve, add 8 oz dressing, toss salad. LEFTOVERS (GF ONLY): Reheat slightly (about 45 sec. total, toss pasta half-way through reheat time) and add additional dressing. Leftover cold GF pasta will absorb too much and get pretty dry.

The warm pasta will soak up the dressing. You’ll need a fair amount of Italian dressing, but add it gradually to suit your taste, because you may not want all that’s listed in the recipe. Just choose a brand that you really like because it is a dominant flavor. I had a few small fresh mozzarella balls in the fridge, so I halved them and added to the salad. I also added a good grind of black pepper, since we’re pepper lovers. Do give this some time to chill in the fridge allowing the ingredients to meld because the flavor does improve. One ingredient that you don’t want to skip is the Parmesan cheese. I think that’s the “flavor bomb” in this pasta salad! We’re not huge pasta salad fans but do enjoy one occasionally, and this is one that I’d make again.

I have been making a variation of this for years, after being served something similar in a restaurant. If I'm in a hurry, I'll add a box of frozen mixed vegetables (green peas, corn, diced carrots & lima beans) that have been thawed. I also like a lot of grated sharp cheddar cheese (sometimes Gouda too!) and always add chopped scallions. I like a garlicky homemade vinagrette - takes 3 minutes with a mini food processor - just mince a clove of garlic, add vinegar & Grey Poupon mustard, salt & pepper and after mixing that, slowly drizzle in your olive oil. Fresh dressing makes the salad "pop"! You don't need much - why pile on claories? I just use a little. In summer I make a lot of this pasta salad, because it keeps well in the fridge and is great to have on hand and serve on a hot day with a green salad.

This pasta is bulletproof. Except for the rotini you can have or delete anything you want. I love Julianne red onions but my wife does not and prefers fresh broccoli.. which I hate! When we make it we do not add any salad dressing at all until we are ready to dish it up and eat. Keeps the pasta from absorbing the dressing and getting gooey. Croutons and bacon bits are excellent additions too.

Easy recipe to follow and quick to make. The grocery store didn't have tri-coloured pasta, so I used Rotini instead. I added mushrooms, broccoli, ham and feta cheese. I cooked the ham and veggies, with the exception of the cucumber and tomatoes, just slightly so they were soft but still crunchy. I also used creamy poppy seed dressing instead of Italian. Kids loved it! Great summer time meal. Will definitely make this again and again.

I heated oil in a skillet with minced garlic (don't let the garlic brown). Added and sautéed carrots, red bell peppers and zucchini squash, so they are slightly tender (lessen the crunch to be more in line with the soft pasta). I then mix together the veggies, pasta and Paul Newmans, and then refrigerate for a couple hours so the flavors can mesh. ***garlic is a must***

This is a great recipe. It's now my husband's favorite side-salad. I was a little pressed on time, so I took a shortcut by putting all the vegetables in my Ninja and processing it for a second or two. The salad didn't look as pretty as it could, but it saved me a lot of time. I also only used about half a bottle of Italian dressing and thought it was great. Additionally, I kept the Parmesan cheese on the side so people could add as they wanted it. We had leftovers for a few days and I think it tasted the best on day 3. Thanks for the recipe, it was easy and a great summer salad.

I've been making this salad for years with a few variations. I only use 1 bottle fat free zesty italian (mid size bottle) then I add garlic powder, black pepper and some salad supreme seasoning to taste. Without these seasonings it was a bit flat. I tend to use the same veggies plus broccoli but is good with any variety of veggies. I've made both with and without cheese and have also added pepperoni and olives, depending on who's coming to dinner. A great hit at potlucks and cookouts (have had requests for it for summer wedding receptions also) I usually make this with tri color spiral pasta but have also made it with spaghetti noodles broken in half....calling it spaghetti salad..generally I use peppers, celery, onion, tomatoes, olives and pepperoni with that version. Add cheese just before serving or will get gunky. I prefer cubed but have used shredded. I make mine the night before, mixing a few times so flavors blend well, then mix well just before serving. This salad has always been a great hit and I will make it for many years to come!

I have prepared this staple and it is always well received but I use canned chopped tomatoes not fresh.Follow the directions in the recipe,substituting 1 large can of chopped tom's for fresh; do not add dressing. Allow the pasta salad to stand overnight (or about 4 hours) in the 'fridge to absorb flavours and moisture from the canned tom's. An hour before serving,add bottled dressing,tasting as you pour and stir(as some commercial dressing is saltier and thcker than others I add a touch of fresh lemon juice to the contents). Add Parmesan or Romano cheese, stir and serve.
I am making this weekend for our end of summer bbq here at our co-op

Love this recipe as an easy weekday meal-prep option! It’s fresh, flavorful, and perfect to take to work for lunch with a protein on the side. I made a homemade Italian dressing to keep it a little lighter and healthier, and it was delicious. Definitely one I’ll make again!
I made this salad buy using a bottle of the apple vinegarette from chik-fil-a. It was delicious. Will make again
This is an easy recipe and very tasty! I used a sweet, white onion and orange bell pepper, that's what I had on hand. Will be taking this salad to a 4th July party, I'm sure it will be a hit!

My changes- I use bottled salad dressing for ease. Half LIte Ranch/Half Lite Italian. Adjust to taste. Try different varieties, peppercorn ranch and different fat preferences. I use FF and always get asked for the recipe. I like to add black olives and crumbled feta cheese.
I made it for lunch. Omitted salami and added some broccoli flowerettes and capers

Really liked the look of this dish, but I agree with others that it was far too much dressing. I only added in 1/2 a bottle and I thought that was plenty. I think this is very versatile and you can change it up to use whatever vegetables you fancy.
So easy! Made it with yellow bell pepper because they didn’t have green at the store. Used Ken’s Northern Italian dressing.
